newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Reverse widening to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Reverse widening to U.S..

text.p: Australian bond yield spreads to the U.S. narrowed slightly on the day, but still remained just above the low levels seen last week.

Comments by Prime Minister John Howard that he would like to see lower interest rates as the government is no longer running such large deficits saw the September 10-year bond futures contract strike a fresh 3-1/2 year high.
This helped bond yield spreads reverse any early widening to the U.S. and saw the 10-year differential edging back to the sub-50 basis point level seen last week.

"The moderate growth and encouraging inflation outlook which support an easing bias in monetary policy suggests that the market has the potential to outperform a little further," said Su-Lin Ong, fixed income analysts at Hambros Bank.
"Once rates appear to have bottomed for this cycle and growth indicators pick up more convincingly, the spread may widen modestly to 70 basis points by year end," Ong added.
